title: The Lion and the Mouse
source: Aesop's Fables, tr. G. F. Townsend (1867), 'The Lion and the Mouse'
lesson: No act of kindness is ever wasted, and no one is too small to help.
lines: A mighty lion was napping under a tree, when a tiny mouse ran right across his nose.
The lion woke up and slammed his paw down. Gotcha!
Please let me go! squeaked the mouse. One day, I'll repay you! Cross my tiny heart!
The lion laughed so hard he rolled over. You? Help me? But he let the mouse go.
Weeks later, the lion got caught in a hunter's net. He roared and roared, but he could not get free.
The mouse heard him, ran over, and chewed through the ropes. Nibble, nibble, snap!
You laughed at me, said the mouse. Now you know: even a mouse can help a lion. No act of kindness is ever wasted, and no one is too small to help.
Next episode: a wolf who needs an excuse. Follow so you don't miss it!
